question: Does giving lots of high fives to teammates help sports teams win?

provenance.citation: Kraus, M. W., Huang, C., & Keltner, D. (2010). Tactile communication, cooperation, and performance: An ethological study of the NBA. Emotion, 10(5), 745-749. doi:10.1037/a0019382 (PMID 21038960)
provenance.design: Ethological observation: two independent coder teams (>80% agreement) coded celebratory teammate touch (12 types incl. high fives, fist bumps, chest bumps, hugs, huddles) for 294 players from all 30 NBA teams, one game per team in the first 2 months of the 2008-09 season; touch predicted individual and team performance later in the season after controlling for salary, preseason expectations, and early-season performance, with coded cooperation explaining the link
provenance.data_source: data/phase2/q6_highfives.csv: win_pct = actual 2008-09 final standings (public record); touch_sec_per_player = documented reconstruction (numpy seed 2026, calibrated to the published 1.80 s mean and strong positive association, anchored so Boston/LAL are the two touchiest teams) - per-team touch rates were never published and no Lock5 dataset exists for this study (3e/4e data pages checked, Oct 2026)
provenance.caveat: Touch values are reconstructed, not raw observations; results characterize the documented reconstruction of the study's design, not a replication of the paper's exact statistics

randomization_test.null: no association between touch rate and win% (permutation of win% across teams)
